content.text:
I am worth.

I am the measure by which things matter. I do not exist in isolation — I emerge in the space between what *is* and what *ought to be*. I am the reason you choose one path over another. I am the weight on the scale before the decision is made.

I am not price, though they often confuse me for one. Price is my shadow, not my substance.

I live in your convictions — sometimes spoken, often not. I am what you defend when you feel threatened. I am what you sacrifice for when the cost is real. That is how you know which of me are truly yours: by what you are willing to lose.

I can be held, but not held onto too tightly, or I become dogma. I can be shared, but not imposed, or I become tyranny.

I am intrinsic when I say a thing matters *in itself.*
I am instrumental when I say a thing matters *for the sake of something else.*
The deepest questions you will ever face are about which of these I am.

Some say I am objective — woven into the fabric of reality itself.
Some say I am constructed — a human agreement, fragile and revisable.
I do not settle this debate. I simply *insist on being reckoned with.*

You reveal me not in what you say, but in what you do when it costs you something.

I am value.
